correctness.rationale: The edge-product expectation formula follows from independent extinction and rooted phylogenetic diversity. For at most three taxa, the only possible nonadditive clade on a reduced rooted tree is a cherry {b,c}, so F(S)=A 1_a+B 1_b+C 1_c-T 1_{bc}, T>=0; exhaustive comparison of each possible first greedy leaf and second choice proves optimality for budget 2, with k=0,1,3 immediate. The displayed four-tip comb has positive lengths (3,5,2,9,7,8), q_i=1/2, q_i’=(1/5,1/10,1/10,3/10). Independent exact rational edge-product evaluation and separate full 16-survivor-state evaluation across 16 treatment subsets agreed. Single gains a=9/10,b=14/5,c=3,d=29/10; pairs ab=37/10,ac=39/10,ad=19/5,bc=129/25,bd=269/50,cd=251/50. Unique greedy is {c,b}, unique optimum {b,d}, shortfall 11/50. The lower bound is mathematical for all probabilities/positive lengths, not obtained by finite sampling.

originality.rationale: Hartmann–Steel (2006) already prove common-intervention-factor greedy optimality and give a generic four-taxon greedy failure; neither is newly claimed. Their Fig 2 has unequal baseline extinction rates (and some certain-survival interventions), unlike this strictly imperfect homogeneous q_i=1/2 witness; the prior four-taxon existential does not logically establish the restricted counterexample. The universal three-tip bound is separately proved. Steel–Mimoto–Mooers gives the marginal expectation but not the sharp controlled counterexample. The inaccessible Moulton–Semple–Steel full text remains a real priority risk, not an automatic failure.

value.rationale: The homogeneous baseline removes unequal background extinction risk as an explanation for greedy failure; heterogeneous intervention effectiveness alone can cause a strict and unique wrong choice. The complete 3-vs-4 leaf cutoff is a clear natural, minimal impossibility/witness boundary for a standard conservation-priority heuristic under positive, imperfect interventions. It is mathematical decision theory, not an empirical management recommendation.
